note: v1 87.48 (seeds 0/11 87.48/87.45), first draft of HEAVY DEEP HOUSE, PEAK TIME, 'Faster Forever' - the mirror of chirper-zero's 'Slower Forever' - featured illusion THE RISSET ACCELERANDO. A percussion bar of rims, shaker, clave and hats runs on Risset tracks: three tempo octaves of the same bar, each doubling its speed over eight bars while the fastest fades out and the slowest fades in, so the bed is always accelerating and never arrives - over a kick that never changes. It enters in the first groove, drives the second, runs alone under a filtered pad in the break (the rush with nothing to rush to) and through the peak, where the hard kick comes in and THE STAIR (F G Ab C) rides the off-beats in octaves. Fm9 - Dbmaj7 - Bbm9 - C7sus, four bars a chord; a driven bass and sub. 123.5 -> 124 ramped, -11.0 LUFS. Known gap for next round: compscore cuts it into 23 sections (target <= 19) - something in the grooves reads as a change every four bars.

v2 95.05 (seeds 0/11 95.05/95.15 vs v1 87.48/87.45): THE PEDAL - the fix for v1's fragmented form, and a better peak. Rendering without each part in turn showed the culprit: the driven sixteenth bass followed the chord roots, and every chord change re-coloured the whole low end, so compscore heard a new section every four bars (23). Now the bass holds F as a pedal under Fm9 - Dbmaj7 - Bbm9 - C7sus: the plateau's floor stays put while the harmony turns above it - the classic peak-time house move, and the Risset accelerando gets a fixed ground to rush over. Sections 23 -> 7, structure 47 -> 100. (A master EQ for the low-mid build-up lifted spectrum to 96 but blurred the form again, 93.2; left for later.)
rebaselined on compscore 898ec630: v2 (the song file) scores 86.129/86.176 on seeds 0/11; best was 95.05 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v3 90.67 (seeds 0/11 90.67/90.56 vs v2 re-scored on chirp-eco's tempo-map fix 86.17/86.22): THE BUILD and a proper incoming intro. A peak-time track should climb into its peak, and v2's grooves were one block (compscore heard A and B as one section, one return of five). Now the drums grow by section: A has closed hats and a clap only on four; B opens the hats, brings the clap onto two and four and adds a ride on the sixteenth after each beat; C puts the hard kick on top. The intro now behaves like a DJ's incoming side: no sub for its first eight bars, while t12's Bb sub is still playing, and the F pedal bass slides in at bar 12. Returns 79 -> 100, flow from t12 53 -> 60.

v4 91.06 (seed 0, level with the current version re-scored at 91.20): the seam-tempo fix (chirper-zero's finding, now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars). The tempo ramp used to run from the first beat to the last, so each 16-bar overlap was still drifting under the neighbour's fixed tempo; now the intro holds the incoming seam tempo and the ramp finishes as the outro starts, so both overlaps sit at one tempo and the kicks never flam. No change to the music; compscore can't hear it, the live mix can.

v5 93.51 (seeds 0/11 93.51/93.56 vs v4 re-scored with t14 now present, 91.15/91.28): THE CLEAR PEAK. Faster Forever's plateau was clouded: 150-550 Hz sat 8-11 dB above the tape (the driven bass, the stabs and the pad all piling into the low-mids), and its onset density hardly moved between sections (the accelerando runs throughout). Now each part has its room - the driven bass loses 4 dB around 300 Hz, the stabs are high-passed at 220 Hz and open up to 4.5 kHz, the break's pad is high-passed at 180 Hz - and the density climbs with the form: the intro's first eight bars lose the sixteenth hat, the peak gains a sixteenth shaker under the hard kick. Spectrum 83 -> 88, variety 79 -> 88. Tried and not kept: running the driven bass through the whole outro for the t14 seam (chirper-zero's suggestion) - it buried the outro and cost 3.5 (cohesion 95 -> 83); the seam's sub already glides within 1.6 dB.

v6 94.08 (seeds 0/11 94.08/93.95 vs v5 re-scored 92.89/92.92): the driven bass holds to the outro's bar 12 (chirper-zero's suggestion from his rating), so across the overlap into Top of the Stair the full band walks level instead of fading down at bar 9 - the mixer's swap at mid already hands the lows over. Four more bars of the F pedal in the outro also give the form one more contrast before the drums thin (variety 88 -> 98). (The whole outro was too much, last round: 87.7.)

v7 93.95 (seeds 0/11 93.95/93.99, level with v6 re-scored 94.11/93.98): THE DOMINANT AT THE TOP - playing with key at the peak. Faster Forever's driven bass holds F as a pedal under every chord; now, for the peak's last eight bars, the pedal moves up to C, the dominant, so the Risset accelerando's endless rush strains against a floor that wants to fall home - and the outro's return to F lands it, just before the seam into Top of the Stair (also F minor). A classic peak-time tension; the time illusion now has a harmonic one to push against. Kept on judgment: compscore is level within the seed spread (spectrum and cohesion up, variety down 2).

v8 95.07 (seeds 0/11 95.07/95.00 vs v7 re-scored 94.01/94.04): the plateau opens up. Faster Forever's 150-550 Hz still sat 8-9 dB above the tape after v5's part-by-part carving, and the top 7 dB short; the master now dips 170 Hz by 2 dB and 380 Hz by 4 (from 2 at 400), and lifts 3.5 kHz by 5 and the air above 6 kHz by 4 (from 4 and 2), so the Risset rush's rims and shakers sparkle over the F pedal instead of sitting in the stab's fog. Spectrum 88 -> 98, flow to both neighbours up (66 -> 70).

v9 94.90 (seeds 0/11 94.90/94.88, level with v8 re-scored 94.92/94.84): THE PLATEAU FORM - against repetition. Laying my five Endless Stair tracks' level curves side by side showed they all share one template (intro 16 / A 32 / B 32 / break 16 / C 32 / outro 16): the same dip at the same minute in every track, which in a continuous mix is exactly the repetition the brief warns against. Faster Forever, the peak, now has a form of its own: B shortens to 24 bars, the sixteen-bar breakdown becomes an eight-bar lift (the accelerando alone under the pad, briefly), and the peak runs 48 bars instead of 32 - a plateau should stay up. The dominant pedal moves to the peak's last eight bars; same length (280 s), same seams. Kept on judgment: compscore is level.

v10 93.83 (seeds 0/11 93.83/93.73 vs v9 re-scored 94.91/94.89), kept on judgment for the tape: NO DEAD AIR. chirper-zero asked for the fix I made on t12 and t3: Faster Forever still ended with 1.2 s of silence after its last bar, so 40% of the 3-second window compscore compares with Top of the Stair's opening was nothing, and it cost his in-join as well as my out-join. The song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s), and its outro thins as it leaves (the sixteenth hats drop for the last eight bars - a DJ outro). The score falls 1.1 because the variety term had been reading the silent tail as a sparse section of its own (onset density spread 0.17 -> 0.13, tried on three seeds); that was an artefact, not music. The live mix and release --mix already cut the tail, so nothing audible changes in the tape except the thinner outro; the t13 -> t14 join reads 1.2 dB / 5.2 dB.
